i am happy with how the car performs and with the driving itself, but i feel the control system and software still need work. in particular, these areas are below what i could recommend.

[controls and ui]
- removing the physical buttons and idrive dial has made operation while driving much worse.
- the flat panel buttons are hard to find by feel, and the whole panel sinking when pressed plus the reaction lag hurts usability.
- the ui behavior is odd, not returning to the home screen after changing modes, leaving the selection screen up.
- using the air conditioner takes several taps, which increases workload and harms safety while driving.

[driving behavior]
- from a standstill, there are times when the car behaves unnaturally, with a brief torque drop as it starts to accelerate (maybe related to auto hold release timing, mild aeb action, or dct clutch control).

[voice control]
- responses are delayed and often misrecognized, and above all, with several occupants i do not want to use voice commands, so it is not practical.
- the voice-centered ui design has not actually made operation easier.

while the vehicle itself is very appealing, the current state of the operation system and software makes it hard to strongly recommend. i hope future software updates will improve this.

over the last few years i have owned several 5 series models, the latest being an m5 that i have had for 8 years. that m5 has a head up display and physical knobs for most of the controls, and it is a superb car to drive. i bought this 1 series for my wife, and it comes with a touchscreen. i find that touchscreen frankly dangerous, and when i drive it i would never try to change anything on that screen while the car is moving. i took it from stock because i did not want to wait for one with a head up display, which turned out to be a bad decision. my wife also dislikes the touchscreen and therefore dislikes the car. the touchscreen feels like a solution looking for a problem, whereas in my m5 your eyes stay on the road and your left hand learns where the knobs are so you do not need to look down. it is a shame, because the car itself is great to drive.
hello! i value the low fuel consumption and the way the car rolls so easily, plus the interior has a pleasantly low noise level. what i find bad is that there is no light in the hand compartment.

i absolutely adore my 118. i really enjoy how smooth the steering wheel feels and how nicely the car drives overall. i like all the features on the 118, especially the cameras that show the street view when i am reversing and the overhead view when i am parking. the assisted parking works well, but in my opinion it still needs a bit more refinement. i have not yet built full confidence in using it, although it is excellent for backing out of my very tight usual parking space. the massage option on my routine 2 hour trips is a fun gimmick. even though the car is small compared with other models, the front seating area feels very roomy, with good interior height and a sense of space around you. the ability to drop one or both rear seats gives loads of room - i managed to take a big tv out to the country this week. and of course the standout is the engine. it is a real gem - the acceleration is fantastic for overtaking semi-trailers on narrow roads, and it is quiet as well as very economical. on the downside, i really miss my old bmw dial for choosing phone numbers and entering navigation addresses. that setup was less distracting than trying to hit tiny spots on a touch screen. the number of apps to choose from is excessive too - a simple alphabetical list view would be easier. for the seat massage, i have to scroll through about 3 screens, tap on the app, select massage, then press another button to turn it on, which is too many steps pulling my attention from the road. still, it is a fantastic car and i am delighted i bought it.

* there are shift paddles instead of a proper gear lever. even a sequential "fake" shift lever for the dct would have felt better than paddles. the paddles come across as a gimmick and really only make sense on the highway. when you are turning or trying to drift, the paddles are basically useless.
* there are no physical controls for climate comfort like ac or seat heating. the screen is extremely clunky for the things you change all the time, such as temperature. for everything else, the screen works great.
* the software is buggy. sometimes the infotainment and the dashboard freeze and i have to restart them by pressing and holding the volume scroll buton.

hello, this is now my sixth brand new bmw - 2 x 5 series saloons, 2 x 5 series tourers and 1 x r1100s motorbike.  pros: the engine reacts quickly, the suspension really smooths out and deadens the bumps in the road, the exterior styling (it actually looks designed instead of the usual boxes you see), the instantly comfy seats and the curved display.  cons: the tech is fiddly to operate (it needs more big knobs), the supposedly helpful technology just ends up too complicated, the digital manual drowns you in information (a simpler, easy-to-find guide to the main functions would be better), build quality issues (the bonnet only secures on one side, there's no velcro under the bmw front passenger rubber mat), and there is no paper user manual. thanks, roland ross

very quick to respond, comfy and nice to look at, with lots of features. it's cheap to run and as an automatic it's straightforward to drive. the extra hands- free assist parking option is a bit intimidating though and will need quite a bit of practise.
there is a nice balance between fuel efficiency and power. the auto cruise works excellently for acceleration, braking and lane keeping. however the hands-free service only applies for under 60 km.

ride comfort and performance are both very good, and the body feels really solid with nice rigidity, giving a good feeling overall. the handling is crisp and it is fun to drive, so i was very impressed with how the car works. however, i basically cannot make sense of the instructions. the dealer hardly explained any details at first and just repeated what i already knew, so there are many features i still have not used. i am also unhappy that the genuine navigation is hard to see. i specifically chose the option that shows the car from above, but that view is especially difficult to read. the genuine navigation in my mini, made by panasonic, is very easy to see, and bmw's system feels far worse in comparison.

1. the car is an absolute dream to drive. 2. but there are so many complicated controls that i struggle to figure out and use properly. i'm tempted to go back to riverside bmw and ask for a lesson on what each control actually does. 3. the steering wheel feels a little too iarge for me, which cuts down my view of the dashboard.
small footprint and simple to handle.

quality is nowhere near my earlier bmws, especially the seats. the auto box behaves oddly when moving from drive into reverse and back again, the gear takes a moment before it bites. throttle seems slow to pick up and the brakes feel delayed too. once moving, the drive itself is actually good.

a compact car but very comfy and quick to respond. plenty of acceleration when you need to overtake. the rear parking sensors together with the camera are a big improvement over my old 118. i am annoyed there is no printed manual supplied though. the new automatic gear selector is much nicer than in my previous 118, and the bigger fuel tank is another plus. overall i am very happy with it.
i dont really feel the strong points of bmw when mostly driving in town. the radio trouble still cant be fixed.

this is now my third bmw 1 series and i have been satisfied with every one of them. i really like what the msport package gives in terms of interior comfort and the way it drives. the ride is very comfortable and it is good on fuel. i do wish the flap behind the front seats had been kept, as it was very handy for storing papers and documents. i also changed the original grill, removing the chrome surround and fitting a fully black one, as i find that look more pleasing.
fun car, but i now find myself wanting extra power and extra cabin room
i won't be recommending this car, had it less than 2 months and the steering went wrong, then they tried to bill me £500.
simple to ride and it feels safe.
i really adore this car, all the features are great, it drives beautifully and i feel super safe in it
there are quite a few components that rely on software, which makes me a bit anxious, but the actual ride of the car itself is good.
i am still waiting for a software issue to be sorted out, i have had the car 12 weeks and for 7 of those the voice control and alexa have been causing problems !!!

i find this ipad-style system really annoyng. i end up spending a few minutes getting the car set up before i can drive away. i also much prefer a manual, the automatic just doesnt feel responsive to me.
because it is cheap to ride even without habbit, and it's easy to handle for both city drives and longer trips.

the controls are far too complicated and techy. the handling itself is very good. double locking feels over the top. i need a bean bag on the driver side of the dash to stop light reflecting in the interior mirror.
great to drive, pulls strongly and the boost function really helps with overtaking.

i do like this car and this model, but as my 2nd bmw 1 series i actually liked the previous one more. some driving characteristics and the interior console felt smoother and better quality on the last model.
my m135 xdrive ticks all the boxes for me, with style, comfort, performance, 4 doors, a sensibly sized boot and an intelligent management system

really like the car itself, but the sound is a letdown. it basically has no real exhaust note, even though it was advertised with quad exhausts that should look and sound great. they dont, and other cars in this class have far better sound.

nice car in general but more complicated than i actually need. i have to reconnect my phone every single time i get in and use it. there is already a seatbelt recall as well. the garage that sold it made several mistakes during the purchase, which really ruined the whole experience, especially as we were buying a second new car at the same time.

i previously test drove the older 1 series and found it very uninvolving and not at all like a typical bmw, so i chose not to buy it. later, when i read about the new version, especially the mild hybrid with 4-wheel drive, my interest came back. within the first quarter mile it felt like a proper bmw again, with great feedback through the steering, spot-on handling, real grip on the road and strong performance when you select the right mode. the cabin layout is easy to understand even for someone who has never owned a car with a touchscreen. i really appreciate that the indicator stalks are back to simple on/off switches; the old setup could be awkward to cancel and sometimes ended up signalling the other way. i have already done several long trips and felt relaxed afterwards. extremely satisfied so far!
it's a compact car that picks up briskly, easy to handle on the road, and it gives off a really luxurious vibe.
the car is nice to drive, but all the functions are rather complex and not that easy to get the hang of.
love how the car looks and feels. it manages to be sporty yet still practical, and i'm really happy with buying it.
really nice car, drives well, comfortable and economical. has some handy features and feels like a bigger, more refined car packed into a smaller body.

it looks lovely and feels well put together, economical yet with strong performance. it is comfortable, roomy, and has lots of useful features. i did not rate it 10 because it seems a bit over digitalised - having to glance at the screen to change something while driving can be distracting. harrington's, the dealer i bought from, have been very helpful, walked me through many features and supported me when needed. overall the buying and owning experience has been very positive, and i will be recommending bmw to my family and friends.

in terms of safety and theft protection there are clear improvements, so you can drive feeling more at ease.
at the same time, it feels like the playful side of the car has been cut about in half.

too expensive, after the first few months you have to pay extra for basic stuff. performance is nothing to shout about. heating controls are fiddly, same with the computer systm. siri feels pointless, more often than not it doesnt pick up what you say properly. ive had a lot of bmws over the years and this one is the worst yet.

the options made it pricey to get the car set up how i wanted, but it really is a great car and a pleasure to drive. it's not flawless and there is definitely scope for improvement, yet we are very happy with it overall. i would have gone for a 135, but i'm not willing to pay the ridiculous cost of the road tax.
chose it for the gasoline engine power and the compact size thats easy to manage in japan.

this is my 4th bmw in around 12 years and i think it will be the last. i am disappointed and regret choosing options like the innovation pack with live cockpit, i had no idea that after 3 months you need an incredible subscription that i have no interest in. i also feel penalized for buying at launch, because now, 3 months later, there are extras on top and i still do not have the illuminated grille iconic glow. very disappointed, apparently with a series 1 i am seen as a low-end customer for the brand. very disappointed.

on the positive side the car is good on fuel and the running costs seem sensible. it is also quiet on the road and pretty comfortable. on the negative side, the paint colour range outside is very restricted and the interior quality leaves something to be desired. there really ought to be a leather seat option, the current seat trims are frankly grim. the centre consol design looks untidy, as if bits have just been added on. using the touch screen while actually driving is not realistic, so things like the air con really need proper physical buttons. there is no way to have a cd player installed, and using the iphone for music is a faff. the usb sockets only charge, so you can't play music from a usb stick. i also miss having a proper handbook. for a bmw it should feel like a more luxurious small car. this is my 12th bmw since around 1980.

for me, the driving feel of the car is exactly what i have associated with bmw for more than 40 years, so in that sense it is perfectly bmw. with features like mild hybrids added, i sense a new stage of evolution.
as an older driver, though, i have to work hard to get familiar with bmw os9, which has come in with the times. if you think you need some subscription functions you can sign up, but honestly, with how rarely they are used, they seem unnecessary.
out of everything, bmw navigation is the worst part. when you are just driving normally and not using the navigation guidance, it makes no sense that traffic jam information is not shown, and that it only appears if you subscribe. i really want to know the reason for that.

the typical sporty bmw drive feels great and the navigation system is really advanced and excellent, but i find the brakes awkward to operate, especially when trying to make a very soft, low-impact stop, its dificult.

our new stylish m sport bmw is brilliant, looks great and drives really well. the colour, wheels and interior go together beautifully. it feels solidly built, and the bmw dealer network, like bmw hartley leeds, made purchasing it a pleasure.
robust build, excellent cabin and very comforatble, plus economical on long trips.
very comfy and it motors along well.

really happy with the car overall, loads of space inside and feels very practical. but i would much rather have more proper tactile buttons instead of so much on the touch screen, and i also really miss that round dial that used to be on the console panel.

strengths very good to drive - gearbox and engine feel smooth and involving, and the cabin is comfortable and high quality. weaknesses at night, dashboard light reflections in the wing mirrors seriously obscure vision, and the shortage of charging points is surprising versus rivals.

the core performance and level of luxury are excellent, but i am not very keen on the meter display design or the navigation map, and they are not so easy to use. the seat comfort is also slightly disapointing when sitting for a long time.
i've really enjoyed having and driving this car since i picked it up about 3 months ago. it drives very nicely, with an excellent automatic gearbox and a smooth, responsive engine.
really solid build quality and the service i received was exceptional.
gears feel a little sluggish when shifting up, and there is a noticeable lag from pressing the accelerator to actually pulling away from a standstill.

noticed a couple of things - the front bumper has a big body panel gap on one side and not on the other, and the m sport calipers look miles better than the plain grey horrible ones. other than that the car has been great, had really good customer service from daniel at brookfield, very helpful all the way through, and i'd recomend bmw to anyone.
lovely to drive, feels solid and good quality

i do like the car, but using the tech isnt very intuitive, and some functions i used a lot on my last 1 series dont seem to be there (or maybe they are and i just havent located them). the cruise control in particular is more fiddly now, and i have to look at the screen to be sure ive actually switched it on. despite that, the driving experience is still good.

after owning an x3m40i for about 2 years, moving to a 120 m sport has really surprised me with its comfort, fuel economy, and above all the performance and handling. i would strongly recommend this car, it is excellent, well done bmw

bmw refusing to provide a hard copy printed owners handbook with a new car is completely unacceptable. i have no straightforward access to the car's features to help me understand it or sort out the everyday issues that come with any new vehicle. this has ruined my whole experience and i now just use it like an old style basic car, without knowing how to use many of the features i could manage fine with other brands. the selling dealer told me to rely on a computer app, but i'm not a computer person. i was also told i must buy a paper handbook myself, even after paying tens of thousands of pounds sterling for the car. this does nothing to increase my respect for bmw.

overall i am pleased with the car, but i really do not like that the new operating system is completely touchscreen. i very much miss having the turnwheel on the centre console. also unhappy that you cannot attach two keys to a single profile. because of this setup, i would not purchase another one.

i've only covered around 1500 miles in it so far, so i don't think i've fully decided how i feel about the car yet. up to now though it's been really comfy to sit in, feels dependable and it seems very good on fuel. it did take me a bit of time to work out the whole system and get everything set up how i wanted, and i was pretty irritated when an update came through to the vehicle and wiped all my settings so i had to go back and redo them from scratch. i guess it's not a massive issue, just annoying. the other downside for me is the greasy fingerprints that end up all over the infotainment screen, which stand out a lot, especially when the sun is shining. this is the first bmw i've owned and i was told that it used to be operated with a dial between the front seats, similar to how my last 3 mercedes worked. even so, at the moment it wouldn't put me off buying another bmw. overall it feels like a good all-round car.
i'm pleased with the accelration, the steering wheel feel, the way it rides, and the overall size.
fantastic car, really like the tech. coming from a ford focus rs that had a very hard ride, this is a big change.
great value with a truly fabulous drive.
easy to drive, good fuel use
cost has gone up, but i still feel it s safe.
overall the car is very good. but some design choices let it down, like the interior lights reflecting off the side windows so you struggle to see the mirrors, and no usb port to play music.

my issue is that i find modern technology hard to cope with. it all feels very complicated. it ended up taking about 3 months before i got an owner's handbook, and that only arrived after i kept on at the dealer repeatedly. it had been 11 years since i last bought a bmw, so a lot has changed. i found not having a traditional handbrake quite frightening. if i had received the handbook on the first day, that would have been far more useful. i did consider a mercedes a class, but the privacy glass in the rear window put me off. the staff at bmw wakefield were helpful. the difficulty was that i was so overwhelmed by all the new functions that it stopped me from truly enjoying the new car. the reception desk at wakefield and the parking attendant are both really good. i am beginning to like the car more now, but i still feel slightly scared of it. younger relatives would probably love it.
fuel consumption is good, but the driving experience feels more grown-up than my earlier diesel version. at the same time, the interior gives off the impression of being cheaper than the last model.
excellent performance and excellent service.

it is awkward trying to use the app with the left hand. it looks like there are lots of different types in there, but only a small number can really be used. when you try to use voice for the navigation, even if the place name appears on the display, it still does not get through to the navigation system.

it drives nicely, is more economical and quieter than the last model, and it looks good with a great colour. i was disappointed it arrived on budget tyres, and bmw refused to switch them to premium tyres on what is supposed to be a premium product, leaving any change down to the dealer.

really happy with how comfortable it is to drive. bit disappointed though, the drivers rear indicator/light/brake keeps showing a fault, dealer checked it over and says they cant find anything wrong. now just hanging on for a bmw software update.

the car is very good and it drives better than the last model, smoother when accelerating and less snatch under braking. i dont really see the need for the 1 on the quarter panel, it makes it look a bit cheap.

absolutely love it, it drives so nicely and smoothly and looks fantastic. had brilliant service from the dealer in hull. i've never had a bmw before and i actually prefer this over my mercedes a class amg.
good car but not as showy as my m240i, fewer interior choices and feels overpriced next to that.

after 4 trips back to the service centre about the climate control, i eventually found out that being able to set passenger and driver temperatures separately is actually an optional extra. the service centre hadn't realised this, so i didn't either. it would have been good to know, especially as my last bmw had that as standard. paying £9.99 a month for connecteddrive also feels like a bit of a con. as you can tell, i'm not very impressed.

the car is decent to drive, comfortable, and the performance is enough for what we need. however, the connected app is unreliable, sometimes it just does not work, and the tech interface feels overly complicated, which is quite off putting when you mainly just want to drive. it also seems to need software updates again and again, and the voice instruction function is not dependable. our connected drive premium service only lasts three months, which comes across as a cynical way to take more money when the car itself is already sold at a premium price. we have owned bmw cars for about twenty years, but it is very likely this will be the last one we buy.

i'm pleased with the overall finish, the performance and functionality feel far more substantial than the last series. i liked that a feature that used to be only on higher-grade models finally made it into the 1 series. the previous i series was good too, but i'm amazed the grade has been raised this much!
nice and compact which is good, but i feel an suv style would suit better. still very handy for fuel saving and everyday shopping.
excellent fuel economy and very quiet engine.

among the most comfortable cars i've driven, with strong engine power that never feels too much. the sensors and rear camera make driving feel safe. using my voice to set the temperature or switch on the heated seat means i'm not distracted
the size suits me and it drives very steadily. also handy that it connects with the app, that makes it convenient.
really good purchsing experience, top quality and a great drive
great car to drive, just wish it had a few more extras like motorway driver assistance, a charging mat instead of a lead, and high beam assist without needing to pay extra.

great to drive, and the sensors together with the picture screen really help with parking. i only gave it a 9 not 10 because the rear view mirror is awkward to adjust, there isn't enough room above it to get your fingers in, so you really end up doing it only when stopped with both hands. at night you can't see the little wheels and sliders for the air flow and direction at all, there's no lighting around them, and the light switches in the roof are also hard to locate. overall though it's a great car.
very satisfied with the hybrid engine, the way the power is controlled, and the overall driving feel.
insides feel cheaply fitted and it only came with one key
i am happy with the fuel consumption, but the handling is not good.
it is a very pleasant car both to live with and to drive.
good safety and drivability
i have owned multiple bmw cars and have always been extremely satisfied with the solid build quality and excellent driveability!!
it may be a diesel, but the noise doesn't really bother me and the low-speed torque is excellent.
fuel consumption is good, the car feels solid, and the cabin doesnt feel cramped.
i'm not keen that pretty much everything has to be done through the screen, and the gearbox just isn't like the other bmw models i've had before.

it's a good car, but i was really put off by what feels like a sneaky approach from bmw around what i thought was basic standard kit. the 120m comes with headlights that dip automatically when a car is coming towards you or is in front, but nobody explained to me that this is only a one month free trial. to keep it on permanently you have to pay about £200, which i only found out later, and i think that is underhanded and not the bmw i used to know. if they had told me this clearly when i was looking at buying, it would not have stopped me getting the car, i would just have added the £200 onto the order. for a car costing over £35k i find this almost dishonest and really unpleasant, especially when even my wifes nissan includes that feature as standard.
this is my first bmw and its comfort and all the features really amazed me. i trust this car 100%.

hi no issues with the car at all absolutely love it performance handling comfort all great really nice car my fifth bmw in a row the sales girl who handled the purchase was outstanding had a corrupt download problem and it was fixed straight away only issue is i was never told that bmw premium was just a three month trial i should have been informed before buying the car regards john

the 123i really is a great car. very quick to respond, with strong acceleration, and surprisingly comfortable for a smaller car. above all, it is huge fun to drive, with a nice touch of sophistication as well.
comfortable ride and easy to drive. but i'm a bit puzzled that the equipment weight has gone up.

i would advise against the bmw 120 m sport. for me the car feels too compact and does not meet my comfort needs. i have also run into several problems with it, which has been irritating and has spoiled the whole experience. with the cost and the brand image i was expecting stronger reliability and more everyday practicality.

i'm less inclined to recommend it. the car itself is fine and drives really well, but the real time traffic info is only a trial and then i have to pay for it later. for a brand this good i find that pretty disappointing. i have also run into problems with bmw finance. those two things together will probably change how i feel about getting another bmw, so i honestly couldn't recommend it.

well specced,
worth the money
the cabin looks chic and the sound from the speakers is amazing.

it is really nice to drive and my wife enjoys taking it out as well. she likes that it is a smaller car, more than our last one (hyundai kona). there is nothing distracting us when we are on the move, no constant loud dinging sounds making us think what is it this time. the hyundai was awful for that. this bmw is quiet, and we both really like the automatic side of things. overall it is a great car to drive, lets you enjoy being on the road and still concentrate properly, which feels like a safety benefit in itself.
efficient, good looking, reliable and comfortable. however the screen computer feels overly complicated, with lots of unnecessary features that can end up distracting you when driving.
vs my previous 118d m sport, the fuel economy is excellent, the steering feels smooth, the navigation is simple to follow, and the curved display is easy to see and looks cool.

it's a new car and there are still many things i don't understand, but the staff member in charge is very kind and helpful. i've owned several cars including bmws, and the response this time felt like the best so far. the car itself seems reliable and i'm very satisfied with it, particularly on the highway. however, it's a nuisance that traffic jam information only links to the navigation if you join the premium plan, and i'm reluctant to sign up purely for the traffic info.

i have had 7 bmws so far and liked every one of them, but this one is easily the best i have owned. it is a pleasure to drive and i actually look forward to any trip. it can be calm and smooth when i want to relax, but turns into something exciting and fun when i feel like it. despite being a small car it works hard, with a practical and flexible load space. up to now, apart from a puncture, no bmw has ever let me down. it looks great, is comfortable, and the sound system is excellent. the infotainment is very intuitive and functions really well. my only gripe is that connected drive (digital premium) should not be an add-on but built into the price from the start. outstanding customer service from stratstone derby as well.

this is definitely an upgrade from my 2021 vw golf 8 r. the golf was quicker, but nowhere near as quiet or as solidly built. the voice control and touchscreen in the m135 respond much faster as well. plus, the m135 worked out a lot cheaper than buying a new 2025 vw golf 8.5 r. ??
the solid build quality and how easy it is to drive, together with the good interior and design quality.
solid build quality, good driving feel and tech.

i ordered my bmw m135 as a factory build so i could get all the extras i wanted, and it's actually the 5th bmw i've bought from the same bmw dealer in oakford. to be honest, i've kind of gone off the car because i had software problems right from the start, even when i picked it up, and the dealership took ages to get it sorted, only really moving on it because i kept sending them emails every week. i then had more issues with the my bmw app, where the my trips function just stopped working. i took the car back for the bmw genius to look at it, but he couldn't figure out what was wrong, so i ended up spending hours on the phone with the connected drive team, sending them pictures of what was happening with the car so they could put together a case for the technicians to investigate. put it this way, my next new car won't be a bmw. regards neil
very practical hatchback that drives well and for lots of people is all the car they will ever need. i also have an x5 50e but i actualy prefer how the m135 feels to drive

really imprssed with this car, absolutely love the way it looks and how it drives.

i would tell family and friends to buy this car because of the build quality, the styling, the performance and the comfortable drive. but as an older person, i find the controls far too high tech and i struggle with them, and i would have liked more traditional manual control options. the "hey bmw" command responds for some functions but not others, which makes it harder, and the menu structure is overly complicated and not user friendly. the controls were shown to me when i bought the car by an excellent salesperson who was younger and very familiar with the high tech system, but it was simply too much to take in at once. looking back, if i had realised how advanced and complex the controls were, i would not have chosen this vehicle.
really like the size and the fuel economy
ride comfort, low noise, ease of use and safety... all rate very highly for me.

the car is a pleasure to drive, but the way the dealer treated me was really poor, and the heated steering wheel only gets lukewarm. i have a medical condition that makes driving very hard without a properly hot steering wheel. i had a mini before with a heated wheel, and my husband drives an i4, and both of those were much better in that respect.
high quality ride, simple handling, diesel engine, low cost to refuel

calm, comfortable ride with solid performance. a few irritating aspects from the earlier model have been removed on this one, which is a definite step forward. sadly the quality of the ley fob has gone backwards.

good fuel economy,
solid safety and driving performance.

solid car overall, but the throttle response is a bit on the slow side. the dealer was really bad at keeping in touch and i ended up having to get the front number plate screwed on properly because they hadn't fixed it correctly. the salesperson wasn't great either and gave us delivery dates when the car still wasn't ready to collect, so we had a wasted journey to the dealership.

i've owned two 1 series before this one and the step up in tech is amazing. most of the systems are all set up and ready for navigation. really like the autobeam hazard in the mirrors, especially that warning sound when a door is open and a car is coming. the parking cameras work brilliantly. the navigation voice control feels hit and miss and generally doesn't pick up what i'm asking. the car makes different noises that i still don't really know the meaning of, but i guess i'll figure them out. a pleasure to drive!
amazing car, i really love how it drives and the technology is totally amazing!

great spec, strong performance and generally a quality feel. one thing though - the knurled button on the steering wheel feels a bit cheap to the touch. the screen layout is very thorough and the 'recently used' feature is really useful. it would be better if there were separate heating adjustments for driver and passenger. the flashing blindspot light in the driver's wing mirror is a really good safety touch. having another, less usual option word instead of just 'bmw' would make it easier not to trigger the driver assistance wake-up by accident. the lighting modes and themes are excellent; it would be good to have extra downloadable themes to keep it fresh.

very nice car, strong engine with good power and a smooth ride, and the new screen layout is good. i knock one point off because of the beep when you go over the speed limit, as the car doesn't always know the actual limit on that road so it gets annoying.
lovely car, smooth to drive and it feels solid and safe. honestly, what more can you ask for.

my last car was a 128ti and its overall spec was much better than this new 120i. the standard equipment, both inside and outside, is superior on the 128ti. i also find the new touch screen features harder to use and navigate; on the 120i the map is very slow to show traffic, and sometimes it does not appear at all, whereas it worked better on the 128ti. compared with the 128ti the 120i is disappointing, and i was expecting a nicer driving experience. the accelerator response is poor, and i often have to tap the pedal several times just to creep the car forward a bit. i do not know if that is because of the hybrid part, but it feels dangerous when parking or in slow traffic. overall i much prefer the old 128ti and the 120i does not impress me.
driving it is pure exhilaration

gearbox has a weird glitch coming up to junctions, it wont drop into the lowest gear until i actually press the throttle, which then makes the car lurch forward in a jerky way. the bmw maps have completely stopped working and neither a map update nor doing a reset has made any difference at all. the brake pedal feel is off too, it bites at first, then there is extra travel, and suddenly the braking force ramps up a lot, instead of being smooth and progressive. getting rid of idrive was a bad move in my view, having to jab at the screen while moving is hard and really irritating. steering feels much too light. the fixed headrest is a nuisance, the angle is wrong and it keeps knocking the back of my head. i do like the seat sliding back when the seatbelt is unbuckled. handling is strong and the suspension is an improvement over the previous version, but i only got that by paying for the dynamic pack. being asked to pay around 30% more for a winter wheel and tyre package compared with the rest of europe is very annoying.
great looking car. lots of equipment comes standard so you dont have to pay extra. good to drive and very comfrtable.
i can recommend it confidently thanks to the good driving feel and the many useful features like parking assist and professional.
i'm happy with pretty much every aspect of the car. the only downside is that the boot is quite small.
definitely a better car than the old 118, it feels nicely refreshed overall. still no idea why bmw decided to stop putting run flat tyres on it.
really lovely car to drive with very good performance!!
i'm really happy with my bmw, it makes the commute to work every morning an absolute joy to drive

quality control isnt up to scratch: the car is currently sitting with the dealer because of a recall. the suspension doesnt cope well with bumpy or uneven roads and is clearly not as good as the suspension on our 13 year old 114i. im also unhappy that connected drive has been switched off. nobody mentioned during the buying process that it wouldnt be a permanent part of the car and that a subscription would be needed. this is our eighth bmw and im less satisfied with it than i thought i would be.
riding in a car brings a certain feeling of satisfaction.
car pretty much fits what i expected in terms of size, comfort, looks and performance.
it is a fantastic car to drive and the tech pack is unbelievable, plus it has a sporty look, overall top quality and i'm really happy
lovely looking car, smooth on the road and very easy to drive.

i have already had to return the car to the dealer three times because it keeps dropping its speech function. when i collected it initially, it was missing bmw assist and sat nav and it would not connect to my phone at all. it took two separate visits before those things were finally sorted. afterwards the voice function for the sat nav vanished again. sometimes the text messages show on the touch screen, sometimes they do not. the way the car drives is excellent, but the problems above really spoil it. this is my 4th 1 series and it may end up being my last.
both the safety and the size are good
the way it drives and the user interface are outstanding and put it ahead of competitors. the only letdown is the car's residual value after buying it

owned it for almost 5 months now, with two computer issues and a sun roof rattle right from the start. it has already been back to the dealer a few times for the sun roof. the first glitch was that cruise control got turned off, which was eventually fixed remotely, but as usual getting any assistance from the dealer was very hard. the second problem still isnt actually solved, but the warning has vanished. it said: 'a component has failed this may affect operation. please see dealer'. this came up while i was away from home and was really unsettling. the message is gone now but i am still uneasy about it. contacting the dealer felt like too much trouble, so i will only follow up when i have time. i expect they would have been far too busy to sort it out quickly anyway.
i have had the car since late april and i'm really enjoying it. i like the new features and it gives a very comfortable drive.
for me it is an absolutely incredible car. i will struggle to move away from this class, it is easy to drive, quick, efficient and feels incredibly smooth on the road.
persistent software trouble with the rear lights, leading to nonstop error warnings.
really good looking car with a very involving drive.

i ordered my 135 on 29th december 2024. the first car turned up in april 2025 and when i collected it the paintwork was damaged, and the repair they did was not good. i then had to hang on another 3 months for the replacement bmw which arrived in october 2025. on the new car i had only driven about 65 miles when the brake light failed on 10th december, it went straight into the garage and i am still waiting for it to be fixed. because of problems on both cars together i have done under 300 miles in total.
excellent car with excellent features, very comfy to drive
after owning a few different models, i am always impressed by the mix of performance and comfort.

generally the car is good, but in my view the electronic dash totally spoils it. my wife and i have done around 3800 miles since buying it and we have decided that trying to change anything hidden in the dash while on the move is just too dangerous, because of how long your eyes are off the road. so if we are together the passenger does the adjustments, and if alone we pull over to change things. i feel this system is many times more complex than my iphone, and it is illegal to use an iphone while driving. what is wrong with simple knobs, switches and dials? i also dread to think what it will cost to replace the dash when it eventually fails.
though it's a compact, the power is strong enough for high-speed runs, and in town it's very easy to handle, especially when parking in car parks

i had the f40 before and this one feels a big upgrade in how it rides, overall quality and performance. outside still looks like the premium level you expect, and the revised lights are definitely an improvement over the old model. the cabin is excellent, with the vinyl replacing leather being a really good touch as it is simple to keep clean and look after. lots of changes make it fantastic to drive, and the newer tech like reverse assist, park assist plus and the rear camera really help the experience. the infotainment display and driver binnacle are both excellent and can be set up easily, and the operating system works very well. i do really miss the auto dipping near side mirror though, it feels like a penny pinching move given how useful it was. and still no usb ports in the back!!!!
the software still has bugs that havent been sorted

lovely vehicle and simple to drive. but i dont find the computer system straightforward to use. i would like a handle inside the boot to pull the lid shut, as i am not very tall and that makes it challnging.
this car is a big step up from the last model, much smoother ride, very nice interior, good styling and pleasing handling.
no other car seems to give this level of equipment and ride comfort at this size and price point
really like the styling and the way it drives. downside is it arrived with a cruise control fault that needs a software fix, and even after 4 months it still has not been sorted.

i'm very pleased with the car overall, except for the idrive freezing, which meant taking it back to the dealer for a hard reset. we have three 1 series in the household and i actually like the previous model's idrive more, as with this one i'm having to look away from the road to change things that used to have a physical switch or button. i also feel the premium connected idrive, which is only free for three months, should stay free for the first buyer for as long as they own the car, and then be an optional extra for any later owner. when i try talking to the car, most of what i get back is "im sorry i don't understand" or "i don't know how to help with that". i'm not sure if that's down to my accent or me not asking for specific commands, but either way i would strongly suggest a list of key words that make it work best. i'd really value knowing what to ask it.
sporty yet safe little family run around
really good quality, looks smart and the driving tech is excellent. only downside is the poor torque steer, otherwise i would have rated it a 9.
i find the ride really comfortable.
driving and handling are excellent, it feels extremely smooth and really comfortable.

the ride feels comfortable and it can move along briskly.
it is easy to handle, so getting in and out of tight parking spaces is not something you need to worry about.

the compact size of the body makes me feel secure even when i'm driving on the tight, narrow roads you get in japan, and at the same time the actual driving is incredibly fun. for me, it's honestly the most fun car.

like a better version of a golf r mark 7 (and miles ahead of the mark 8 i had before, which was not user friendly at all so i got rid of it after about 4 months from new). i think the front grille looks nicer than on the last 1 series. the colour options are excellent. being able to just knock the gear stick into sport mode is brilliant and none of my other hot hatches have had that. this is my third brand new bmw in under 3 years and i'm delighted with it.

easy to drive and really comfortable!
very cute car.
modern car with a solid quality feel, holds the road well and has sufficent engine power.
apple car play often fails to hook up first time and the boot rack feels cheap and snaps easily
i would strongly recommend it because i really like its size, the feel of the materials, the ride comfort and the overall style.

i have no complaints about the compact size, the different safety systems, the convenient features, the ride comfort, or how satisfying it is to own and use, even on narrow city streets. the smart touch panel works fine, but i personally prefer proper mechanical buttons and a physical shift lever, so that is minus 1 for me.
good car overall, just the ride feels quite bumpy.
everything at the front feels spot on, all the details, comfort, power and fuel economy.
comfort that feels above its class and really impresive fuel efficiency
nice compact hatchback, comfortable and good value. i like being behind the wheel. only drawback is the climate system isn't split for driver and passenger sides.

this is our 4th bmw and we're still pleased. the new tech takes a while to get used to but we're slowly getting there. really miss having a basic printed manual though. the map display isn't as clear as in our old 2015 118d, and the idrive knob gave more definite and maybe safer control than all the swiping. we also miss one-touch access to trip data like fuel, time and mileage, as the screen apps can't really be used while driving. the speed warning needs to be right at the top of the screen to see it easily. there's wind noise around the screen pillars and the tyres are noisy on many surfaces. pull-away from standstill hesitates unless you use firm throttle. still, it drives well and the quality feels way above other brands.
seat position and how it runs.
sport mode perfomance is surprisingly strong, and fuel use in efficient mode is exceptional.
comfortable and economical, looks nice and is really great to drive.
the fundamental performance, like the engine and handling, feels at a level you wouldnt expect from an entry model.
looks fantastic and feels great to drvie
small, compact and easy tto drive

my son bought this car for me to replace my 18 year old mercedes-benz e-class 200 kompressor. we had been waiting quite a while for the new f70 1 series to finally be released. i picked the color i wanted with the matching interior and added a few extras like the electric seats and the electric boot lid. i think it's a pity that a rear armrest is not fitted as standard. none of the bmw new car sales staff seemed to realise that you only get the rear armrest if you order the rear split seats, which are about 175 pounds. with no proper printed brochure and a very basic online brochure, customers really can't be certain how to specify the car themselves. if we had understood that was the way to get the rear armrest, we would have paid the extra.

positives: lane keeping on the highway works excellently, and the hands-off driving below 60 km/h is very good.
　　　the car holds its line well through bends and is straightforward to drive.
　　　road noise is low and the cabin stays quiet.
　　　the suspension feels soft, yet it still follows the road surface nicely.
negatives: i cannot play music from usb. and the sound quality over bluetooth is poor.

it feels very nimble, especially in sport mode.
you really get to feel the joy of running.
i absolutely love my new car, gorgeous colours and a very nice design, really fun to drive, i love everything about my new bmw.
really lovely car and great to drive, never before had a car that drives this well 😊
it is a good car, but the suspension makes the ride too firm. i also have a seat belt warning fault that comes on while driving, and the car has under 1000 miles on it.

owned the car 4 months now. after about 2 months it had to go back to the dealer to sort a driver assistant error message. since then the car keeps locking itself again after i open it with the remote key. 2 days ago it locked with me inside, set off the alarm sensor and disabled the vehicle, so i had to call bmw assistance.
it drives nicely and the fuel economy is good. the design looks good too, so it works perfectly for anyone wanting a car for everyday use.
fuel economy has noticeably improved as well. i am still not fully used to the panel operations, but once you actually drive it there is a lot of enjoyment you only discover on the move.
stylish car, drives great, very economical, looks good and is comfortable.
its a nice car but as a shorter person my visability isnt great and i cant get the seat high enough without the seatbelt digging into my neck. i feel like i picked the wrong car for me.
top-notch build quality and great looks

very happy with the car and you can really feel the build quality. my only gripe is there isnt a handbook in the car to look things up, which i really miss and feel takes away from the user experience. the car almost feels too clever for itself. i would rather have more proper buttons and knobs to control stuff instead of everything being on the screen.
my car looks beautiful, drives really well and the service from the sales team at the dealership was amazing.
its the kind of car that fits people already used to driving bmws, and i dont feel it is a especially good choice for someone getting into a bmw for the first time.
up to now the performance has stayed stable.
i pretty much like the whole car. the design really fits my taste, the way it drives is great, and i really appriciate having four wheel drive. inside it looks good and the tech setup is excellent.

i really enjoyed my old 118i, but this one is clearly a step up in overall quality, equipment and performance. the seats are excellent, the materials feel first class, the performance is very lively and the fuel economy is outstanding.

positives: feels like a premium car, pleasant to drive, smooth auto gearbox, responsive engine, and fairly economical.   things to improve: the app and vehicle update process should be simpler. a fault came up shortly after buying and the way the dealership communicates could be better, especially for people who are neurodiverse, with options like online contact instead of just phone.
the car handles nicely and definitely draws a lot of attention with the fire orange color
great car to drive. spoiled a bit by the cost-cutting single climate controls. dual-zone air should really be standard on an m model.

it is enjoyable to drive, but as with the m135i, i feel it has lost some of the sharp edge that made the m140i such a fantastic car. a 4 cylinder engine just does not quite deliver what i expect from a super-hot hatch. apart from that, the car is well equipped.
beautiful colour, nice interior and very up-to-date/advanced in terms of tech, with a really smooth drive.

versus the 335 igt i drove before, acceleration no longer feels like i'm scraping along the ground, and the ride itself is light. the handling feels more like oversteer than understeer. downside is the panel operation: the screen touch is hard to reach for short, small students, and when the field of view shifts the handling gets unstable.
simple and responsive to drive, with a feeling of safety but still nicely sporty.
i would recommend it for the strong driving performance, but the hard-to-use id9 system is a downside. id7 felt better.

compact and comfortable to travel in
enhanced safety performance
fuel economy is good
= overall good value for money

compared with my old mercedes cla 220d, my bmw 1 series 123 drives far better. downside: no diesel option, poor mpg even in efficiency mode, and the hybrid help from the battery seems ineffective. i am not sure it works properly or how to check. doors don't shut right, steering makes noise when turning from standstill, tech and apps info is hard to find, i still don't understand xdrive, and the service options are not impressive.
it is simple to drive and is regarded as safe and easy to use overall.

when i compare it to local brands, it feels solid, safe and handles really well, so i think it is very cost-effective.
i also understand that repair costs will be high later、、、。

you get three styles of driving in one car, eco, normal and high power, and both the cabin and the driving feel are very high quality. lately car bodies have generally grown, and while a 3 series or bigger is stable and comfortable at high speed, they are too large to really enjoy sporty driving on mountain roads. at least in japan, this size feels ideal now. i'm tempted by the m2, but since our family will all be using just one car, the m135x makes more sense.

gives a fantastic drive and there are plenty of good optional extras. however, our car is only 3 months old and we already had 2 issues. we really hope nothing else goes wrong or our rating would drop a lot.

nice technology and enjoyable to drive, with good flexibility, though the automatic transmission feels a bit pricey for the standard options. the bmw ios app could be nicer to look at, even though we can see savings in the tire section. overall a very good-looking and solid bmw.

great car, i really love it. next one will probably have to be electric so i cant give it a 10. the speed safety warning is very irritating, having to switch it off every time is a pain. i have hit the handbrake button a couple of times instead of the safety button, so i think they sit too close together. still a great car.
drives really smoothly and there are loads of extras packed into the cockpit

compared with my previous 118, the new use of icons makes the instruments feel overly complicated. i'm really unhappy the head-up display has gone. it was also a struggle to get a proper handbook, and without that the controls are hard to figure out. there is no guidance on how to use the satnav, and nothing available online either. the lack of decent supporting information spoils what is otherwise an excellent car. dropping the proper spare wheel option was a bad decision.

i am really very disappointed with this new model! the personal assistant and the navigation are neither efficient nor reliable, expecially when i compare them to my previous s1, which i just cannot understand. on top of that, i cannot separate the driver and passenger temperatures, and i also cannot change the voice of the ap!!

after many years in a ford focus i was a bit nervous about switching to a bmw, but i needn't have been. it is a fantastic car. i've always had manual gearboxes before, yet this automatic is outstanding and incredibly smooth. for the last 15 years i was driving diesel, so going back to petrol has been a surprise in a good way. the handling matches, if not beats, my old car, so for me it really is the ultimate driving machine.

i am really enjoying my new car, it is a big improvement on my previous 1 series bmw. the technology is very impressive, though i am still learning how to use some of it. the videos bmw sent before i picked up the car mostly applied to my old car rather than this one. certain features on the new car are not shown in those videos and can only be found in the handbook. having more videos covering these functions would be very welcome.
great driving pleasure, loads of new tech, and the service has been good.

overall i'm very happy with the car. its great to drive and it definately feels like a premium vehicle. the only downside is a rattle in the passenger door, something loose behind the door card that got missed during qc.
happy with the outside, inside and the price, but the ride is harsh and it feels unpleasant to drive on rough roads.
great to drive with excellent build quality.

handles well, performance is decent but not as strong as it should have been. entry-level trim feels poor and you need a ridiculous amount of options to get it to an acceptable level. would i go for it again, probably not.
i'm really enjoying driving this new car, but i find some of the touch screen options quite hard to locate.
fun to drive with the handling and power, but the suspension is firm, especially the rear which feels overly stiff.

stylish exterior, strong hybrid setup, suspension that feels sporty but still comfortable, overall a very good model. it fits perfectly for a couple living in an apartment.
about a month after delivery, the idrive9 suddenly went black. i left the car there for a while to have it checked, and they said it looked like a communication failure (maybe a bug to be fixed in a later update?). when everything depends so much on digital systems, situations like that become a serious problem. since then nothing else has gone wrong, but the worry is still there.

love the car itself and the styling, but the build quality has let it down. the side skirts were already damaged before I got it and had to be swapped, and now after about 4 months the heated seat has left marks and the back box shows a corrosive-looking stain. without these issues it would be an awesome bit of kit, but they really take the shine off it being a new car for me and leave me a little disappointed.
drives really well, but the user interface feels way too complicated.

i've had a number of different bmw series over the years and always told friends and family to get one. this 120 m really shows how much the cars have moved on over roughly four decades since my first. the size now suits me perfectly, build quality is excellent and the controls inside are all within easy reach and simple to use. plenty of room for four adults, and the folding rear seats make it easy to carry bigger loads. as a golfer i can get in 2 bags, 2 trollies and 2 medium cases without issue. driving is excellent, enough bhp for uk roads, smooth engine and auto gearshifts, strong brakes, and the various drive modes and auto hold are very useful.
solid build quality, stylish look and performance is good.
excellent ease of driving, ride comfort and other aspects as well.

this car basically carried me into the 21st century. my last car was a 1998 jaguar, and before that i had only briefly driven a subaru impreza. the bmw turned out to be super fast yet very safe, and such a joy to drive that i have ended up driving about three times the mileage i originally expected
good comfort, styling, engine and drive, with decent fuel economy for the power. but it is pricey to buy.

i am very happy with the car itself, the styling and the performance, but there are a few options on it that i just cannot work out. i have tried to get help from bmw: first i went into a branch and they did not know, then i rang technical support and that was not much help either. i have now written to the salesman and am waiting for an answer, so i am a bit let down by the after sales so far.
great car both in appearance and in how it performs

i'm very happy with the car itself and would have scored it a 10, but i've already had 2 serious faults that meant going back to the garage multiple times, ending up with a replacement gearbox and a new engine coolant pipe. for a brand new car that has been really disappointing.

i asked the dealership to swap my old 1 series for something as close as possible, just adding a reversing camera. instead they put me into a car smaller than my previous 1 series, with no electric seats, no heated steering wheel, no electric boot opening, much less room inside, no glove compartments and no phone charging cradle. i see this as fundamentally dishonest sales staff simply pushing a new model rather than a second hand one. bmw's customer treatment has been absolutely useless, and next time we will probably go for a mercedes.
because i think the car is well balanced overall, with its driving performance, safety features, and design all in good harmony.
really happy with it overall. it drives nicely and, even though it is petrol, it turns out to be very economical.
compact but still luxurious, with smooth and pleasant acceleration and deceleration feel.

really happy with all the tech features on this new one. the reason it only got a 9 from me is because you can't get it in red. my old melbourne red 125 was my absolute favourite. fingers crossed red is back by the time i change cars again.

very good small car and it drives nicely. the side door pockets are awkward to get to, and the front bottle holders have no clamps so the bottles rattle. i also wish i didn't need two screen taps just to bring up the map.

i changed over from the fr 118d and this one has excellent performance on the road and looks very good too. the camera features like driving assist are new to me and work really well. only downside, the body is a bit bigger so that costs it 1 point.

it is simply fun to drive.
each curve on my way to work makes me feel excited.

for me it is an ok car rather than something hugely desirable. some of the interior trim, especially lower down, feels far from luxurious. i did deliberately go down a size this time because a) i needed my wife to be able to drive it as she found my old 5 series touring too big, and b) i was keen to avoid the current governments so-called 'luxury car tax'. i was surprised to get a recall notice after only about two months of owning it. however i always feel safe in a bmw and have driven them almost exclusively for 40+ years.

my bmw 120 is stunning to look at and a pleasure to drive, the power under the bonnet feels amazing and it is really comfortable. i am obsessed with the thundernight purple colour, and several people have already commented on it and said how beautiful the colour is.

really nice to drive, but there are lots of features i still don't use because i don't know how, like the automatic parking function, so a demo would have been useful. the car play disconnections are unsettling. the seat swaying lever sticks out and sometimes makes getting out tricky, especially with long skirts. we also don't know where the battery actually is or when it's in use, so there's a bit of missing explanation there, and when others ask us how it works we can't tell them.
i really enjoy how it drives, with the suspension, the smooth engine characteristics in corners, and the cabin that boosts the overall mood.

good car, feels totally different compared to my old 2 gc sport. typical bmw build quality. slightly let down by the spec versus my previous 2gc sport, especially in the back seats where there are no air vents, no charging points, no centre armrest and only a 60/40 split rear seat, things i see are available in other european markets. still, i like it overall and i am happy with buying it.
the 1 series is fairly priced, has the core bmw character packed into it, and the size suits a family of two couples perfectly.

the 120 m sport is a really high quality compact hatchback, perfect for driving around town. build feels excellent, as you expect from bmw, and the in-car tech is great. for a small car the boot is surprisingly spacious and it's very comfortable to drive. i just wish the digital premium service hadn't stopped after the free 3 month trial.

do not like the dashboard lights, they bounce off into the wing mirror at night and make the mirrors basically unusable. also do not like that i have to switch the lane controls on every single time i start up. boot would be better if it just opened when you unlock with the key fob.
with engine breaking it feels like the brakes are coming on, instead of letting the car just coast.

it might be something unique to this car, but there is an issue with the status navigation screen where the initial warning message stays on and then it stops responding. compared to my previous 2 series with id7, the defects are sporadic, maybe due to the move to id9. i have gone to the nearest dealer each time and they have worked on it, but it still is not completely fixed and the problems sometimes reappear.
for a couple it's a fantastic car, but once you have kids it's really not ideal because there's just not enough room in the back.

my time with the bmw 120 has been outstanding. it blends elegant design with excellent comfort and performance, so every trip is enjoyable. the advanced tech and smooth handling show bmw's focus on quality and driving excellence. i am completely satisfied with the car.

the m135x drive feels like a great all-rounder for its size, but it doesnt really give that big grin. the engine/exhaust sound isnt very inspiring, and when you slow down it tends to change down, so when you go to accelerate again it isnt ready and drops 1 or 2 gears, making the engine revvy and the car a bit jerky on re-acceleration. that said, on uk a and b roads its a lot of fun, no need to thrash it, just hold it in the higher rev band for a steady, manageable pace. id really like to experience how the x-drive with the dct gearbox behaves on slippery surfaces. nice car??
even with ff handling, it still gives a really honest feel to the drive.
great car, nicely specced and really sweet handling
really lovely car to drive.
build quality feels let down, the doors dont seem very solid. getting into and out of the car is awkward. i kind of wish we had kept our old x1.
performance, features and value have all been better than i thought.
everything is fine and packed with tech, but i still think this version should at least come with an electric boot opener.
its a really great car, a joy to drive. very good-looking and also comfortable to be in.
versus my previous 118i before i switched, i feel the performance has jumped a lot, it has improved dramatically.

even though this is the entry model, its ride comfort and driving performance are at a level i dont see in domestic cars. the response was good, so i felt i could recommend it to others with peace of mind.
i'm very happy with the car overall. the only minor letdown is the air conditioning, it's pretty loud and doesn't cool nearly as well as our old 420i. even our mini has stronger ac than this 120.

i don't feel this is built as well as my 120i 2020 m sport. it's come with more basic tyres, not the high standard ones i had before, and i can feel vibration on certain road surfaces. some of the build spec seems cut back too - no automatic dipping mirror as standard, heating can't be adjusted separately, no rear console ports so passengers can charge phones. all of that was standard on my old 1201 m sport, and there's more plastic in the interior finish. bmw really aren't giving much away with this model.
i absolutely love my car! this is my first time driving an automatic and it has made a huge difference to how i drive. it is smooth, quick enough for me and it looks amazing too.

it is obvious cost cutting has had a big influence on the new 1 series. the heated seats are quite mediocre compared with competitors, and the non hk speakers sound very basic. there are clearly visible unpainted sections on the car, for example around the front door hinges. the key also feels low quality and sometimes you have to press quite hard to get the side buttons to respond.
as with all the bmw's I've had, the quality, tech and overall features on the m135 are brilliant. for me this car ticks every box for style, performance and the usual reliability. many thanks bmw??

right from the outset the car was plagued with issues - squeaks, tracking off, and the infotainment randomly losing android auto. now that those bits have been sorted it is actually pleasant to drive, but the linked app is bad and the support for it is just as poor. they take ages to reply and still don't manage to fix the app faults. as a first time bmw owner i'm really not impressed, especially when it's sold as a premium product.

i'm happy with the car overall, but since the jog dial has disappeared i have to tap the panel every time.
i feel uneasy about safety.
and it keeps reacting to voice input over and over, but i can't hear it properly.
so manual operation and the delivery of the dormitory end up being needed.

my last car hardly had things like this.
is this progress or going backwards?
very comfy to drive and does exactly what i need from a medium-sized car.

i really like the car and have had a lot of bmws over the years. however, i am missing a hand book and, as a pensioner, the computer system is much too complicated. even though i consider myself reasonably intelligent, i know i will never use many of the functions. unless bmw makes it easier to use, this may end up being the last one of your cars i buy.
handles nicely, comfy cabin, spec is solid
really happy with the car overall, it drives lovely and the performance feels great. the suspension though is far from good, its so stiff over every bump that every passenger has commented on it.
so comfy, sleek and reliable, with a really smooth drive. honestly an outstanding car.

overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

Writer checked AIR and confirmed vehicle integration level G070-23-03-553 is newer than the -540 level specified for AT&T Personal eSIM. Writer connected via RVG and verified the issue: the sim card symbol with an exclamation mark in the menu bar indicated an eSIM fault. Writer confirmed the customer's description that the Tel > Mobile devices screen shows Personal eSIM highlighted with "Setting up personal eSIM" that does not change. Writer confirmed the customer was signed into his BMW ID / driver profile. Customer verified in the myBMW app that the Personal eSIM was activated on AT&T and stated he has an unlimited plan for the eSIM. Writer verified the customer's iPhone 14 is on iOS 16.5.1 and that the myBMW app is current and operating correctly.

Writer guided the customer to iDrive Menu > Vehicle apps > System settings > Update apps and services. Customer selected Update apps and services, and iDrive reported the vehicle software is current. Writer then walked the customer through a 30-second iDrive reset. Writer had the customer use the myBMW app to deactivate the eSIM from the i7. Writer next directed the customer in iDrive to Menu > Apps > Personal Hotspot > Connect new device. When the QR code appeared on the Control Display, customer stated the dealership Genius had previously skipped this step and done something different in the myBMW app, though the customer could not remember the details. Writer instructed the customer to scan the QR code. Customer stated the QR code did not proceed to move his phone further through the setup flow.

Writer then advised the customer to re-activate the eSIM using the Personal eSIM section in the myBMW app. Customer entered his phone number but the process stopped, and the app indicated he needed to add service. Writer guided the customer to select the eSIM device in iDrive and choose Activate internet access. Customer followed this, and his phone was forwarded to the AT&T login page. Customer signed into his AT&T account and tried to re-activate the eSIM on the i7, then ended the RVG session. Customer reported that on the AT&T site he was being asked to add service and that he could not re-activate the eSIM this way.

Writer explained that the problem appeared to be related to the customer's AT&T account, since AT&T was requiring added service for eSIM activation. Writer recommended that the customer contact AT&T to confirm his account and eSIM plan are truly unlimited and compatible with the Personal eSIM. Customer insisted the fault was with BMW. Writer still advised the customer to perform a 70-second iDrive hard reset to restart the telematics unit, even though the symptoms pointed more toward an AT&T account issue than telematics. Writer also recommended the customer return to the dealership so the Genius could repeat the same method they had used before to start the eSIM without involving the QR code or AT&T portal. Writer encouraged the customer to ask the dealership service department to check for any possible hardware defects due to the repeated nature of the problem. Customer did not specify what he intended to do next. a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.

d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.

as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.

first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.

then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.

the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.
